text:
Jackson LaCombe has become Anaheim's workhorse. He's playing 26:54 a night, up from 24:15 last season, and is on the ice for 82% of the Ducks' power-play chances (65% a year ago). The result is 22 points in 21 games, 13 of them on the power play, and all but one an assist.

The five-on-five picture is far less flattering. The Ducks hold just 38.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and they're much better without him. His points are being propped up by finishing around him: Anaheim has scored 7.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on, and on-ice luck like that fades. Last season told a different story; Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for driving chances, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him setting up shots at a 98th percentile rate. So the passing is real and the role is real. The question is whether the even-strength results climb back toward last year's, because the point pace leans heavily on the power play.
